summary.headline: Hubtown guides FY27 pre-sales of ~6,000 crore and collections of ~3,000 crore; 25 South/Downtown debt expected to fall at least 35% by end-FY27.
summary.overview: Management hosted its Q4 and FY26 analyst meet, focusing on the promoter-entity mergers, project launches and debt reduction. In FY26 the company sold about 1 million sq ft, mainly in Mumbai, for roughly 4,400 crore of pre-sales and collected about 1,900 crore. About 11,300 crore of unrecognised revenue from booked sales sits in existing projects, with substantial recognition expected in FY27 on project completions. Two of the three promoter-entity mergers are NCLT-approved and the third awaits exchange approval. Refinancing of the roughly 15% legacy debt has slowed due to Middle East market conditions, and the proposed equity placement at 341 was cancelled in favour of a possible QIP.

financial_highlights.change: Management said both pre-sales and collections improved vs previous years; no exact percentage given

financial_highlights.value: approx. 1 million sq ft, primarily Mumbai

financial_highlights.metric: Unrecognised revenue from booked sales (existing projects)

financial_highlights.change: Construction finance for 25 West from ICICI at 12%

segments.name: 25 South / 25 Downtown (merging entities)
segments.commentary: 25 South is about 95% sold and expected to complete in FY27; 25 Downtown has sold almost 1.1 million sq ft of carpet area. Combined debt of these two is about 4,000 crore and management expects at least 35% reduction by end of this year.

segments.name: 25 West (Bandra)
segments.commentary: Fifth tower launched, selling about 1,40,000 sq ft; first tower completion expected next year. Construction finance from ICICI at about 12%.

segments.name: Rising City (Ghatkopar)
segments.commentary: Phase 1 (about 6.5 lakh sq ft): 5 of 6 towers have received OC; 6th tower OC expected in calendar 2026. Phase 2 (commercial offices) to be partly launched this year.

segments.name: Hubtown Seasons (Chembur)
segments.commentary: Phase 2 launch of about 500,000 sq ft expected this year, including a strata commercial building, one luxury and two mid-luxury buildings; phase 1 revenue expected in FY27.

segments.name: Mulund-Thane (Sunstream City)
segments.commentary: About 150 acres on seafront at Thane and Mulund, about 2.5 crore sq ft, not yet launched; environmental clearances being obtained and expected within months.

segments.name: Commercial (Gujarat and Pune)
segments.commentary: Four ongoing commercial projects in Pune, Ahmedabad, Mehsana and Baroda; three Gujarat projects expected to recognise substantial revenue this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales guidance of around 6,000 crore and collections of around 3,000 crore.
Surplus collections to be used first to repay high-cost debt; at least 35% of combined 25 South and 25 Downtown debt expected to reduce by end of FY27.
25 South expected to complete this year; 25 West first tower next year; 6th Rising City tower OC within calendar 2026.
Launch pipeline this year: 25 Vistas (Thane), 25 Estates (Khalapur weekend homes), Seasons Chembur Phase 2, Rising City Phase 2 (partial), and a fifth tower at Mahalakshmi.
Management says returns to shareholders and stakeholders will start coming from FY27 onwards.
Mergers: 25 West and Ghatkopar holding entity merger expected this year; 25 South/Downtown awaiting exchange approval. Effective date of all mergers is 1 April 2025.
capex_capacity: Land bank of about 350 acres and over 35 million sq ft; delivered 47+ projects, mainly in MMR.
Total ongoing and unlaunched pipeline stated as in excess of 1 lakh crore GDV; 25 Downtown and Sunstream each about 40,000 to 50,000 crore.
Launch-pending projects (excluding Sunstream) estimated at about 50,000 to 60,000 crore GDV, mostly on the floor per management.
Substantial increase in construction activity this year, which absorbed most of the cash outflow; approval and sales expenses also elevated.
Project funding taken for Seasons Chembur Phase 2 and 25 Estates to support launches; debt rose slightly this year as a result.
demand_pricing: Management says walk-in inquiries have not declined despite the slowdown; 25 Residences sold about 5,000 crore with zero advertising, per management.
Borivali product reportedly selling at 50,000 to 60,000 per sq ft; management expects prime-location products to hold demand.
Rising City Phase 2 commercial offices expected to do well given strong office market.
Management said price growth cannot be expected to be sharp, but prime-location product should avoid a cycle hit.

qa_highlights.question: Why does pro forma financing cost look high relative to combined debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest payable to DLF on Downtown's balance sheet was unprovided for 3-4 years due to disputes; it is now provisionally booked after settlement. Some further outflow until full repayment; Shapurji's share was small.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 15% cost of borrowing be refinanced lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Refinancing efforts continue but have slowed due to the last six months' market conditions and the Iran-US/Middle East situation; not expected in the immediate future.

qa_highlights.question: What is the year-end FY27 debt level for 25 South?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is combined across 25 South and 25 Downtown, not only 25 South; at least 35% of the total should go down by end of this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total GDV of the launch and pipeline projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Total including unlaunched and ongoing projects is over 1 lakh crore; 25 Downtown and Sunstream each about 40,000 to 50,000 crore; other launch projects about 50,000 to 60,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What happened to the equity placement at 341 per share?
qa_highlights.answer: It was cancelled because the market did not support the preference share issue; management is now looking at a QIP instead.

qa_highlights.question: Has the 6,000 crore asset-debt raise authorised last year been done?
qa_highlights.answer: No, not raised yet; the company is still trying.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sunstream City plan and financing?
qa_highlights.answer: About 150 acres on the Thane/Mulund seafront; environmental clearances are the main hurdle and are expected within months; capital needs and financing will be planned after approvals.

risks_watch: Legacy debt at about 15% cost; refinancing stalled amid Middle East conflict and market conditions.
Unresolved exchange approval for the 25 South / 25 Downtown merger.
Sunstream City depends on environmental clearances for the seafront site; no launch timeline.
Equity raise: 341-price placement cancelled; QIP plan unconfirmed. The 6,000 crore asset-debt enabling resolution remains unused.
Collections guidance (3,000 crore) is well below pre-sales guidance (6,000 crore), so collection execution is key to deleveraging.
Management did not give a clear FY26 collections growth figure or FY27 operating cash flow number.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, project delivery and the merger roadmap, but cautious on financing: refinancing is on hold and fundraising has shifted from preference shares to a possible QIP. Some answers were loose, including a GDV figure the management said it could not reconcile to the investor's number.
key_quotes: And so that's the strength that the product has, that's the stren gth that the relationships we have built with our customer have.
We are on a track to ensure that the debts remain under control.
I assure you that the returns to the shareholders and returns to all the stakeholders are will start coming up from 27 onwards.
